name: Zippor
title: Father of Balak, king of Moab
summary: Zippor was the father of Balak, king of Moab, who feared the people of Israel as they approached Moabite territory after leaving Egypt. Zippor is primarily known through his son Balak, who hired the prophet Balaam to curse Israel. The name Zippor means 'bird' in Hebrew.

keyEvents.title: Balak identified as Zippor's son
keyEvents.description: Balak, son of Zippor, was king of Moab at the time when Israel camped on the plains of Moab after defeating the Amorites.

keyEvents.title: Balak sends for Balaam
keyEvents.description: Balak, son of Zippor, sent messengers to the prophet Balaam to curse the people of Israel because he feared their great numbers and strength.

keyEvents.title: Zippor mentioned in Balaam's prophecies
keyEvents.description: In Balaam's oracles, Balak is repeatedly referred to as "son of Zippor", which highlights Zippor's dynastic role in the royal house of Moab.

keyEvents.title: Zippor mentioned in Joshua's speech
keyEvents.description: Joshua reminds the Israelites that Balak, son of Zippor, rose up against Israel and sent for Balaam to curse them, but the Lord turned the curse into a blessing.

keyEvents.title: Zippor mentioned in the Book of Judges
keyEvents.description: Judge Jephthah refers to Balak, son of Zippor, in his diplomatic message to the king of the Ammonites, reminding him that Balak did not wage war against Israel.

keyEvents.title: Reference in Micah's prophecy
keyEvents.description: The prophet Micah reminds the people what Balak, son of Zippor, planned and how Balaam answered, so that they may know the Lord's righteous acts.
